title: An immutable invoice

blocks.text: Every `java.time` class is **immutable**: `plusDays`, `with(...)` and the rest never change the object they are called on, they return a new one. The API is also **null-hostile**: it throws `NullPointerException` for a null argument instead of accepting it. Write your own value class the same way.

items: `Invoice(LocalDate issued, int termDays)` creates it. A `null` issue date is refused right here with a `NullPointerException`.
`LocalDate issued()` and `int termDays()` return what it was created with.
`LocalDate dueDate()` is `issued` plus `termDays` days; if that day is a Saturday or a Sunday, the due date is the **following Monday**.
`Invoice extendedBy(int days)` returns an invoice with the same issue date and a term `days` longer. The invoice it is called on does not change.

blocks.text: `TemporalAdjusters` has an adjuster for "the next Monday".

cases.says: The due date is the issue date plus the term, and extending the term gives an invoice with the later due date.
A due date that falls on a Saturday or Sunday moves to the following Monday.
Extending returns a new invoice; the original keeps its term and due date.
A null issue date is refused with a NullPointerException when the invoice is created.

concepts: A fluent call such as with(TemporalAdjusters.next(MONDAY)) only has an effect when its returned value is kept.
Every java.time object is immutable: plus and with return a new object and leave the original unchanged.
java.time is null-hostile, throwing NullPointerException for a null argument, and a value class built on it refuses null the same way.
